documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for her yearly. They've been trying for a year now, since last August, timed with an ovulation app the last few months. No pregnancy, no late periods. Cycles every 28 days like clockwork, 4-5 days of bleeding, light cramps on day one only. No pelvic pain, no pain with sex. Taking the prenatal daily. Husband healthy, has never been checked. Frustrated but not down. Has had both COVID shots.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: wine is down to almost none. Never smoker.

O: vitals as charted. Well. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Deferred pelvic today, normal last year.

A/P
1. Infertility, 12 months trying, age 32, regular ovulatory cycles. Given two prior chlamydia infections and PID with admission last year, tubal disease is the main concern. Referral to gynecology for infertility workup (expect HSG and semen analysis for husband). TSH and CBC today.
2. Preventive: flu shot this fall. Pap current.
PHQ-2 1. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Referral to Obstetrics & Gynecology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reason for referral: infertility, 12 months of unprotected intercourse without conception.

32 yo G0, regular 28-day cycles, no dysmenorrhea or pelvic pain. History of chlamydia x2 in her twenties, outpatient PID ~2014, and admission April 2020 for chlamydial PID (no TOA). On prenatal vitamin only. NKDA. Mother had endometriosis with hysterectomy at 42; maternal aunt with unexplained infertility.
TSH and CBC pending, will forward.

Thank you for seeing her.

documents.title: Labs and gyn referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your thyroid test and blood count are normal. The gynecology referral went out Tuesday; their office should call you to schedule. If you haven't heard in two weeks let us know.

documents.title: RE: Labs and gyn referral
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They called, first appointment is October 21. Long wait but okay.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation — Infertility
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 10/21/2021
Referring: primary care physician

Reason: primary infertility.

Ms. Pereira is a 32 year old G0 who has had regular unprotected intercourse with her husband for about 14 months without a pregnancy. Menses every 28 days, normal flow. She denies intermenstrual bleeding, painful periods or pelvic pain. Prior sexually transmitted infections: chlamydia twice and an episode of PID requiring admission in 2020.

Surgical history: none.
Medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with endometriosis, hysterectomy at 42; maternal aunt with infertility of unknown cause; father hypertensive.
Social: second-grade teacher. Never smoker. Occasional wine.

Exam: well woman, normal vitals. Abdomen benign. Normal external genitalia and vagina, cervix without lesions, uterus normal size and mobile, no adnexal masses or tenderness.

Hysterosalpingogram performed in our office today (cycle day 8): normal uterine cavity. Neither tube fills beyond the proximal segment; no intraperitoneal spill on either side.

Impression: infertility, tubal factor, with bilateral tubal occlusion on HSG, consistent with her history of pelvic infection.

Plan: referral to reproductive endocrinology to discuss options, which with both tubes blocked will center on IVF. Semen analysis for her husband will be ordered by REI. Continue prenatal vitamin.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given L deltoid. Pt asked whether flu shot is OK if she gets pregnant; told yes, recommended in pregnancy. VIS given.

documents.title: Pharmacy Immunization Notice
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Community pharmacy immunization notification. Patient: Pereira, Melissa, DOB 04/04/1989. Vaccine: COVID-19 mRNA (Pfizer-BioNTech) booster dose, 0.3 mL IM, left deltoid, administered 11/13/2021. Lot on file. No adverse event reported at 15 minutes.

documents.title: Fertility clinic
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The fertility clinic can't see me until April 20. Is there anything we should be doing in the meantime or anywhere faster? Kind of discouraged.

documents.title: RE: Fertility clinic
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm sorry, the waits for reproductive endocrinology are long everywhere right now. Nothing medical needs to happen before then; keep taking the prenatal vitamin. Ask them to put you on the cancellation list. If you want to talk any of it through before April, book a visit or call.

documents.title: Reproductive Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: reproductive endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside reproductive endocrinology and infertility practice
Date of visit: 04/20/2022

Dear colleague,

I met Melissa and her husband today for infertility. She was referred by gynecology after about 14 months of trying; they are now at roughly 20 months. Cycles are regular, every 28 days. Her husband's semen analysis this month is normal in volume, concentration, motility and morphology.

Pertinent history: severe pelvic inflammatory disease two years ago that put her in the hospital on IV antibiotics, plus earlier chlamydia. No surgeries. Medications: prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Family history of endometriosis in her mother and infertility in a maternal aunt.

Vital signs stable. Pelvic examination unremarkable.

I reviewed the hysterosalpingogram from October: both tubes are occluded proximally with no spill.

Assessment: tubal factor infertility, bilateral, after pelvic infection. Male factor absent; ovulatory.

Recommendation: with both tubes blocked, IVF is the treatment that gives them a real chance. We went over the process, timeline, success rates at her age and her coverage. They would like time to think it over and will call us.

Reproductive endocrinology

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know we met with the fertility doctor. We've decided to hold off on IVF for now, it's a lot to take on with everything this year. We may come back to it. Thank you for getting us there.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. That's a reasonable choice and the door stays open. I'm here if you want to talk it through.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 to 8 hours as needed for pelvic pain or menstrual cramps, with food

medications.sig: Take 1 active tablet by mouth daily continuously; skip the placebo week

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia; suspected endometriosis

documents.title: Annual Physical and Pelvic Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, and she wants to talk about pain.

Since about April, aching low pelvic pain most days, a 5 out of 10 today, much worse the first 2-3 days of her period when it can keep her in bed. New this year: it hurts deep with intercourse, enough that they've mostly stopped. Around her period her stools go loose, no blood, no black stool, normal between. No fever, no discharge, no urinary symptoms. Has been taking 400 mg ibuprofen OTC with partial help. LMP 7/12, normal.

After the REI visit in April they decided to hold off on IVF. She is not trying to prevent pregnancy but with blocked tubes doesn't expect one.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, OTC ibuprofen. NKDA.
FH reviewed, mother with endometriosis.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, a little tired. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic and bilateral lower quadrant tenderness, no guarding or rebound, no masses. Pelvic deferred to gyn, who she'd rather see for that.
Urine hCG negative in office.

A/P
1. Pelvic pain with dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia and cyclic loose stools, ~3 months. Pattern and family history point toward endometriosis. Not infectious by history. Start ibuprofen 600 mg q6-8h prn with food. Start a combined pill (ethinyl estradiol 20 mcg / norethindrone acetate 1 mg) taken continuously, skipping placebos, for suppression; reviewed clot warning signs, she's a nonsmoker with no migraine with aura and normal BP. Back to her gynecologist for exam and imaging.
2. Health maintenance: flu shot and updated COVID booster this fall. Pap due 2024.
PHQ-2 1.

documents.title: Pharmacy Request — Early Refill
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Insurance rejecting refill of ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1/20 as too soon (plan allows 1 pack per 28 days). Patient taking continuously, needs 1 pack per 21 days. Please submit quantity override or rewrite sig.

documents.title: Quantity Override Submitted
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called PPO pharmacy benefit line. Quantity override requested for continuous use, dx pelvic pain/suspected endometriosis. Approved for 13 packs per year through 08/2023. Pharmacy notified, filling today.

documents.title: Pain
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update: two months on the continuous pill and the 600s. Honestly maybe a little better but not much, still having bad days. Gyn appointment is Oct 24. Should I do anything different before then?

documents.title: RE: Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. Stay the course until gyn sees you; they'll examine you and likely get an ultrasound. Make sure you're taking ibuprofen with food, and not more than 4 doses a day. Fever, vomiting or pain that's suddenly much worse means call us the same day.

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound. Uterus retroverted, normal in size and contour, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium thin and uniform. Right ovary normal in size with normal follicles. Left ovary normal in size with normal follicles. No adnexal mass or cyst. No hydrosalpinx. No free fluid.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-Up — Chronic Pelvic Pain
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 10/24/2022

Melissa returns, seen last year for infertility (tubal factor, bilateral occlusion on HSG), now with half a year of pelvic pain that peaks with her periods. She describes deep pain with intercourse and loose, non-bloody stools that come and go with her cycle. For the past three months she has been on ibuprofen and a continuous combined pill started by her PCP, with little benefit.

Meds: ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1/20 continuously, ibuprofen 600 mg as needed, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Vitals normal. Abdomen soft without peritoneal signs. Speculum normal. Bimanual: retroverted uterus; tenderness in the posterior cul-de-sac; no adnexal mass.

CBC and inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) normal. Transvaginal ultrasound today normal.

Assessment: chronic pelvic pain with dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia and cyclic bowel symptoms, consistent with endometriosis (clinical diagnosis; strong family history). Normal imaging does not exclude it.

Plan: continue continuous combined pill and ibuprofen for now; recheck in about six months. If pain persists, diagnostic laparoscopy for diagnosis and excision.

OB/GYN
